{{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Based on one of the world's oldest weapon designs, this Tenno-crafted weapon can be used both in stealth and in open combat. The Paris uses a chargeable magnetic field to launch arrows capable of impaling enemies to walls.}} The '''Paris''' is a [[Tenno]] bow that focuses on {{D|Puncture}} damage. Simple to use, it is one of the first [[Primary Weapon]]s new Tenno obtain from the [[Awakening]] quest, alongside the [[Braton]]. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Characteristics== This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage. {{Advantages|class=Bow|}} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow|}} {{WeaponComparison|Mk1-Paris}} {{WeaponComparison|Paris Prime|header=n}} ==Acquisition== The Paris's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Enemies will notice missed arrows but arrows that hit are silent. *Arrows have a large amount of momentum, allowing players to pin enemies to walls. However, a dead body will not lose its momentum if it hits a closed door, so the body will fly through it as soon as the door opens. ==Incarnon Genesis== {{Transclude|Paris Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}} {{Transclude|Paris Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}} ==Tips== *As one of the player's choices for their starting [[Primary Weapon|Primary]] weapon, the Paris will likely be their first introduction to Bows, and weapons with a charge mechanic in general, allowing them to learn how to both use and mod weapons like it. **The primary fire input must be held for the weapon's listed charge time in order for shots to deal maximum damage and velocity. Arrows loosed before a full charge will have reduced velocity, and use the "Quick Shot" stats shows in the [[Arsenal]] rather than the "Charge Shot" stats. ***Not ''every'' shot needs to be fully charged, however; quick shots can be used to quickly kill groups of weak enemies, such as [[Grineer]] [[Lancer|Lancers]] and [[Butcher|Butchers]]. Charged shots can instead be saved for more durable foes, such as [[Eximus]]. ***On weapons that charge before firing, modifying the [[Fire Rate|fire rate]] stat will increase or decrease the weapon's charge rate accordingly, something further augmented by a special mechanic with Bows where fire rate mods have their effects doubled on them. For instance, [[Speed Trigger]] will allow the Paris to pull back arrows near-instantly, while [[Critical Delay]] will make it take much longer. **The Paris's arrows have physical travel time, necessitating the user leads targets both horizontally and vertically outside of close-range engagements in order to compensate. [[Terminal Velocity]] can be installed on the Paris to compensate, ideally in its [[Exilus Mods|exilus]] mod slot. **Maintaining a charge ahead of a combat encounter can make engaging a group of enemies easier. Most charge weapons, such as the Paris, can continue charging and holding a charge while [[Maneuvers|sprinting, sliding, aim gliding]], and using most prompts involving the Use key. Hard landings from falling too far will also usually not interrupt a charge. ***Charging can be cancelled without releasing the arrow using the reload button (Press the reload button while holding fire). ***Using elevators and opening co-op doors does not cancel the charge, however hacking consoles and opening lockers will. So will picking up a holdable item that forces you to switch to your Secondary weapon, such as power cells in [[Excavation]]. **The Paris relies more on high damage-per-shot over volume of fire, unlike the Braton. Misses are more punishing, while accurate hits are more rewarding. While the player should always aim for headshots with most ranged weapons, the player especially should with the Paris to ensure each shot does the maximum possible damage. ***This makes the Paris especially ammo efficient relative to the size of its ammo reserve capacity (the standard 72 arrows of most Bows). The player will thus rarely run out of ammo for the weapon unless it's especially under-modded for the current mission. If more ammo is needed regardless, a rank 1 {{M|Arrow Mutation}} is usually more than enough to keep ammo topped off. **Weapons like the Paris are normally capable of hitting more than one enemy per shot in some way; in its case, its charged shots have 2 meters of punch through. Positioning yourself to hit multiple enemies in a line, or using abilities such as Mag's Pull to clump enemies together, can allow you to damage or kill more than one enemy per arrow, compensating for the weapon's low rate of fire. ***This punch through also allows the Paris's arrows to be shot through thin walls and still hit an enemy, or through physical shields such as a [[Shield Lancer|Shield Lancer's]] shield. *The Paris's damage being weighted primarily towards [[Damage/Puncture Damage|Puncture]] means it will deal more damage towards [[Corpus]] enemies especially, though its high damage relative to when the weapon is obtained means it will generally perform well against any faction. Its precision nature makes it well-suited to bypassing Corpus enemies' shield gating by taking them out with single headshots. **[[Damage/Magnetic Damage|Magnetic]] or [[Damage/Toxin Damage|Toxin]] damage can be added to the weapon to further increase its lethality against Corpus enemies, though this is generally unnecessary until the player has progressed a few planets into the [[Star Chart|star chart,]] as Corpus are relatively frail even without faction damage bonuses (or Toxin's ability to bypass shields). *The weapon's high critical chance but low status chance make it well-suited to mods that increase the former (and with it, critical damage). A max-rank copy of [[Point Strike]] alone will increase the Paris's critical chance to 75%, causing every three arrows to be critical for every one that isn't, on average. **The Paris's Puncture weighting means that it will often apply Puncture status to enemies when it successfully procs a status effect on hit. Puncture's status effect both decreases the victim's damage output and increases how likely they are to take critical hits by a flat value, up to '''80%''' and '''25%''' respectively at the maximum count of '''5''' stacks. This can further increase the Paris's critical output, but only if its low status chance allows the effect to proc in the first place. *The Paris, being a Bow, is considered "Silent" when firing; enemies will not react to the sound of arrows being loosed. This makes the weapon ideal for the greater use of stealth in early-game Warframe compared to other Primary weapons; [[Exterminate]] missions can be completed without the player taking any damage, and [[Spy]] missions pose a much lesser risk of data vault alarms being triggered. **While other early-game Primary weapons can have [[Hush]] installed to become silent, most lack the Paris's affinity for killing in a single shot. Enemies killed by Bows, such as the Paris, also tend to cause the victim's corpse to be impaled by the arrow and fly along with it until it hits a wall, displacing it and reducing the likelihood other enemy patrols will see it. ==Bugs== *After charging an arrow and firing it while zooming, the next arrow you fire will not be drawn from the quiver, and instead the Paris and your hand will jerk very slightly. The next shot will show the reloading animation correctly. ==Trivia== *Paris is most likely named for Paris of Troy in Homer's Iliad, who was a skilled archer and the one to have killed Achilles by firing an arrow into his heel. *The Paris is the only bow that does not have a tension spring, as the arrow is held in place and launched by magnetic induction rather than physical force. *The Paris is modeled after a [[wikipedia:Bow shape|decurve bow]]. ==Media== ParisBowCodex.png|Paris in Codex. Paris (1).png|Paris as shown in the arsenal Paris (2).png Paris (3).png Paris (4).png|The quiver for Paris {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|Uub7Mjer8nk|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{Ver|34}} *(Undocumented) Mastery Rank decreased from 3 to 0. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Paris {{ver|29.1}} *Fixed Paris bow 3D draw sound not cutting off when bow is fully drawn. {{ver|25.7}} *Normalized quick shots to have the same critical chance/damage and status chance as charged shots. *While reviewing Bow stats the team has also refreshed all their FX (including the Lenz)! *Quick Shot increased from 120 to 160 *Charged Shot increased from 180 to 320 {{ver|22.12}} *Mastery Rank increased from 0 to 3 *Charge speed increased from 1 to 0.5 secs {{ver|19.10}} *Paris model reworked. {{ver|7}} *Introduced. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Mk1-Paris}}, the [[Mk1]] counterpart. *{{Weapon|Paris Prime}}, the [[prime]]d counterpart. *[[Paris Incarnon Genesis]], the Incarnon power-up for the Paris series. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Paris]] [[es:Paris]] [[fr:Paris]] [[Category:Bow]] [[Category:Tenno]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Update 7]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Puncture Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Silent]] [[Category:Single-Shot]] [[uk:Паріс]]

[[Category:Launcher (Primary)]] {{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|The Penta Launcher fires up to five grenades that can be remotely triggered at just the right moment.}} '''Penta''' is a Grenade launcher used by {{Faction|Corpus}} [[Penta Ranger]]s and [[Vambac|Vambacs]]. It launches ballistic grenades that can be manually detonated with [[Alternate Fire]]. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Blast}} damage. *Can only have five grenades out at once. **Extra projectiles generated by [[Multishot]] will count towards the limit of five live grenades. *Grenades explode in a '''4''' meter radius upon impacting a surface or enemy. **Initial hit and explosion apply [[status]] separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. *Can use the Penta-exclusive {{M|Tether Grenades}} and {{M|Napalm Grenades}}, as well as the launcher-exclusive mod {{M|Adhesive Blast}}. *Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. {{Advantages|class=Launcher| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. **{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Launcher| *Grenades have slow travel time and heavy arcing. *Grenades have a high bouncing capability which makes it hard to stack on a desired spot. **Can bounce off teammates or companions. **This can be countered with {{M|Adhesive Blast}} which will make the grenades stick to any surface. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 50% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Secura Penta}} {{WeaponComparison|Carmine Penta|header=n}} ==Acquisition== The Penta's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. Alternatively, it can be acquired from completing the [[Jupiter]] to [[Saturn]] [[Junction]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *Detonations can be triggered while the player is performing other actions. *The launch/flight of a grenade is silent (though the actual explosions are alarming, obviously). *Grenades have no arming delay, and can be detonated instantly with the use of the Secondary Fire button. *Grenades can be bounced around corners, off walls, and over low obstacles. **Grenades that continuously bounce into enemies will deal impact damage with each collision. **Grenades do not bounce when striking water, coming to a dead stop instead. This allows for easier setting of traps. *Increasing the Magazine size of the weapon '''does not''' increase the 5 grenade limit. *Though the grenade explosion '''does not''' destroy rockets from [[Bombard]]s, impacts by the grenades from very accurate (and lucky) shots can. *With [[Multishot]], the second grenade is usually indistinguishable from the first, as they follow the same trajectory simultaneously and bounce in the same direction. They can be "separated" with negative accuracy from {{M|Heavy Caliber}} at a high enough rank. ==Tips== *Grenades fired from the Penta are lobbed in a heavy arc, allowing the player to kill enemies hiding behind cover much more easily, as the detonation happens upon external trigger. *Standing at a greater height allows for the grenades to be lobbed and bounce further, allowing the user to see the grenades better, as well as eliminating the worry of stagger. *A maxed {{M|Firestorm}} increases the blast radius from the initial 5 meters up to 6.2 meters (6.64 with [[Primed Firestorm]]), allowing more enemies to be caught in the blast. *It is not recommended to use [[Punch Through]] mods as grenades can often go through the floor on some tilesets, making it impossible to bounce every time. *{{M|Split Chamber}} can spawn a sixth grenade provided that the multishot procs when 4 grenades are already out **While multishot mods are commonly considered necessary to increase damage output, due to the Penta's mechanics of careful detonation and limited grenades active at once, it's not as much of an instant damage increase as with normal weapons. It can be useful for setting up a large number of grenades faster, however. *Elemental mods such as {{M|Hellfire}} are external from the main [[Blast]] damage, allowing the weapon to have 3 separate elemental combinations. *Players can detonate grenades in mid-air to score headshots on targets below. *The default color of the grenades can make it hard to see in the middle of a crowd of enemies or from their bouncing. Changing energy color can help with certain tile sets (e.g. do not use bright white for [[Corpus Outpost]] missions). *Grenades will immediately explode when they hit [[Blunt]]s, water surface, puddles from Tar-Mutalist Moa or [[Tectonics|Bulwarks]]. ==Trivia== *''Penta'' derives from the Greek prefix of "''five''", which may refer to its magazine of 5 grenades. **This seems to be the first [[Corpus]] weapon to be named after ''Greek'' origin instead of ''Latin''. **It could also be derived from the explosive compound [[wikipedia:Pentaerythritol_tetranitrate|PENTA]]. ***Notably, PENTA does not usually detonate upon impact or ignition, but rather needs an external explosive trigger, similar to the Penta's grenades. *The Penta (and its variants) are the first and currently only weapons for which the magazine becomes visibly larger as magazine capacity is increased. With high enough capacity the magazine will even protrude out from the bottom of the magazine feed. *The Penta formerly used {{M|Rifle Ammo Mutation}} instead of {{M|Sniper Ammo Mutation}}, despite still using sniper ammo. This was fixed in {{ver|17.5}}. **{{ver|32.3}} made it so that it cannot equip {{M|Sniper Ammo Mutation}} after {{ver|32}} ammo changes. *The Penta was one of the first weapons with a non-static model: The magazine feeds up to the gun upon firing and the slide around the barrel are pulled back during reloading actions. *The Penta was the first Corpus weapon to focus on explosive weaponry, followed by the {{Weapon|Lenz}} in {{ver|21.3}}. *The grenades are flat and rectangular, which is odd, considering their ability to bounce. **Prior to {{Ver|23.2}}, the {{M|Tether Grenades}} augment changed the grenade model to be a short cylinder with concave ends. It still used the default grenade texture, which looked strange but was normally obscured by the grenades's blue glow. **{{M|Tether Grenades}} now causes the grenade to spin towards the enemy instead of staying flat. * Prior to {{ver|18.5}}, {{M|Adhesive Blast}} caused grenades to explode after a set amount of time. *This was the first weapon to have the Zoom capability replaced with a different function pre-{{ver|17}}. *The [[Arsenal]] interface used to label only the damage of the grenade projectile impact, but now labels the {{D|Impact}} damage of the projectile as well as the base {{D|Blast}} damage seperately ('''350''' base). ==Bugs== *In its Arsenal UI, it does not display its trigger function, though it functions as ''Semi-Auto'', possibly because it deals damage on impact, unlike other Active trigger weapons. ==Media== Penta (1).png|Penta when equipped in the Arsenal Penta (2).png File:PentaReinforcements-Website.jpg|Penta Reinforcements image Penta-warframe.png|Penta in Codex Penta Grenade Base.jpg|The default grenade of the Penta with default colours. Penta Grenade Tether.jpg|The grenade of a Penta equipped with the Tether Grenades augment prior to Update 23.2. {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|uuSoGrvlpbM|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|OAb2TU3c-as|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 5 Ammo per Pick Up: *Penta ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|27.3.16}} *Fixed Penta grenades becoming stuck when Napalm Grenades is equipped, thus rendering the Penta unusable. As reported here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1174244-penta-grenades-getting-stuck-causing-the-weapon-to-be-completely-useless/ {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Penta: 50% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|25.7.3}} *Fixed an issue where some projectiles wouldn't come to a complete stop and would slowly float away (noticed on some bouncing Penta grenades). {{ver|23.2}} *Fixed viewing the Penta in the marketplace (specifically the Penta Shock-Camo Skin) resulting in the ammo in the gun taking a second to load upon viewing it everytime. *Fixed the Tether Grenades Mod distorting the look of grenades {{ver|22.3}} *Penta grenades will now bounce off the Blunt. It has a similar behavior as hitting a Grineer. {{ver|21}} *Fixed an issue with the Penta grenades not detonating in succession while switching weapons with Adhesive Blast equipped. {{ver|20}} *Penta Alt-Fire mode now has stats in the Arsenal. *To improve performance, added a small delay between each explosion when activating the alt-fire on certain weapons (e.g. Penta). *Fixed the Tether Grenade Mod for the Penta cancelling Self Damage. {{ver|19.10}} *Fixed unintentional DoT from Adhesive Blast on the Penta. {{ver|19.0.5}} *Fixed Adhesive Blast causing the Penta projectile sound to not play. {{ver|The Silver Grove}} *Penta series damage increased in Conclave. {{ver|18.5}} *Increased AoE damage of the Penta in Conclave. *Increased the ammo pool of Penta series in Conclave. *Penta explosions visual FX have been updated, and will now be based on the player’s energy color. *Fixed the Adhesive Blast Mod causing Penta weapons to detonate after a certain amount of time. used in PvP. {{ver|16.4.5}} *Fixed the Penta not being affected by Volt’s Electric Shield. {{ver|14.5}} *Fixed issues with blank “Trigger” types in the UI for Penta. {{ver|14.2}} *Penta ammo capacity reduced from 540 to 20. {{ver|14.1.3}} *Penta shots fired from Hall of Mirror clones will no longer display weapon trails. {{ver|13.7}} *Improved the performance of the Penta on low end computers. {{Codex|Completely overwhelmed by Infested biology, this former Quanta now fires organic ordinance and a harpoon like appendage.}}
The '''Paracyst''' is the completely {{Faction|Infested}} version of the {{Weapon|Quanta}}. Primarily a burst-fire weapon, the Paracyst possesses an [[Alternate Fire]] mode that allows it to shoot tethered spores at enemies, dealing damage and dragging them towards the player's position. This is the weapon of choice for [[Mutalist Alad V]].

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals {{D|Toxin}} damage.
*[[Alternate Fire]] shoots a single tether to pull in enemies.
*Innate {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarity.

{{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
*Tied with {{Weapon|Burston Prime}} for second highest [[status chance]] of all burst-fire rifles, behind {{Weapon|Kuva Hind}}.
*Large magazine size for a burst-fire rifle.
*Second fastest [[fire rate]] of all burst-fire weapons, behind Burston Prime.
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
*Second lowest base damage per bullet of all burst-fire rifles, after {{Weapon|Burston}}/{{Weapon|Hind}}/{{Weapon|Kuva Hind}}.
*Linearly less efficient – sometimes a target may only die with 4 bullets, which requires an entire second burst to be fired or the Infested Harpoon.
*All projectiles have travel time.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Paracyst's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Bio Lab|Bio Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*Spore pull can interrupt enemy casting/power animations, including the charge-up for [[Railgun MOA]]s.
*The secondary fire ragdolls enemies it hits as it pulls them to the user. Enemies that are hit gain a yellow aura that prevents them from being grabbed again until they recover.
*Adding [[Punch Through]] to the weapon does NOT allow the hook to grab and pull multiple enemies; instead, it will grab the last enemy that it can't punch through, and attempt to pull them.
*When the secondary fire is used in conjunction with {{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}}, each doppelganger will also fire their own spore capable of grabbing and pulling in an enemy.

===[[Alternate Fire]]===
*The Paracyst's secondary fire mode fires an Infested spore attached to an energy tether that can pull enemies towards the player.
**Enemies hit by the harpoon suffer from a damage over time effect that lingers for '''4''' seconds, dealing '''5''' ticks of {{D|Toxin}} damage. 
**The secondary fire mode has a maximum range of '''50''' meters. While the harpoon will still hit and reel in enemies up to its maximum range, it will only pull them to around half of its range.
**Spore pull can also 'pull' humanoid flyers (such as [[Hellion]]s) down, and pull enemies that are stunned by Warframe powers.

==Tips==
*Enemies can be pulled into bottomless pits or inaccessible areas, killing them instantly.
*Modding for {{D|Corrosive}} and {{D|Heat}} statuses will allow the Paracyst to strip upwards of 90% of enemy armor. This can be increased further by the use of {{Resource|Emerald Archon Shard|icon=Emerald Archon Shard}} or {{WF|Hydroid|icon=Hydroid}}'s [[Hydroid/Abilities#Passive|passive]].

==Trivia==
*The spores fires on normal attacks are colored by the player's color scheme, while spores shot with the secondary tether attack are grey and otherwise colorless. This can be seen when shooting them with {{A|Navigator}}.
*The name may be a combination of "Parasite" and "Cyst." [[wikipedia:Parasitism|Parasite]] is commonly any organism that invades a host to drain nutrients, much like how the Infestation is a parasite to the Quanta. [[wikipedia:Cyst|Cyst]] refers to sacs filled with fluids and other materials that expel when opened. This could be in reference to the Paracyst's alt fire.
*The Paracyst closely resembles the tentacle-like structure of [[Jordas Golem]]'s supposed mouth.
==Known Bugs==
*Secondary firing mode is listed as burst fire, despite actually being a charge firing mode.
*{{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from harpoon.

==Patch History==
{{Scrollbox/Article|
{{ver|31.5}}

'''Pax Bolt''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] for a [[Kitgun]] that increases [[Ability Strength]] and [[Ability Efficiency]] for the next ability after a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] kill.

==Effect==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! Rank !! Ability Strength & Efficiency
|-
| 0 || 7.5%
|-
| 1 || 15%
|-
| 2 || 22.5%
|-
| 3 || 30%
|}

==Acquisition==
Can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|10,000}} per arcane upon reaching the rank of '''Old Mate'''.

==Notes==
*[[:Category:Channeled Abilities|Channeled Abilities]] (e.g., {{A|Exalted Blade}}, {{A|Renewal}}) that are activated during the Pax Bolt buff will keep the [[Ability Strength]] bonus on them for as long as they are kept active, even after Pax Bolt has expired.
**This does '''not''' apply to the [[Ability Efficiency]] part of the buff. The bonus Ability Efficiency will be removed and updated the moment that Pax Bolt expires.
**Subsequent Pax Bolt buffs will temporarily reduce the energy drain for any currently active channeled abilities for the duration of Pax Bolt. Whether this is intentional or not is unknown.
*Similar to other [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] kill conditions, the enemy must be killed by a headshot through weapon damage, and not any damage-over-time [[Status|status effect]] such as {{D|Slash}}.
*The Ability Strength and [[Ability Efficiency]] gained are '''additive''' with other mods. For example, a Warframe equipped with maxed {{M|Intensify}} and receives a Rank 3 Pax Bolt buff would have +60% Ability Strength.
*Note that [[Ability Efficiency]] still caps out at 175% even with Pax Bolt equipped, though channeled abilities use uncapped values.
*Works oddly with Wisp's [[Reservoirs]]; the bonus strength will apply, but if the player already has a weaker mote active, touching the new buffed mote will simply refresh it rather than change its strength. In order to take full advantage of Pax Bolt, you must wait for your current buffs to expire.

==Trivia==
*Inscription on Pax Bolt is [[Solaris Language]], reading "BAWLT" forming the sound "Bolt".

;ARCANE STAT CHANGES PER RANK

In short, there are three stats that each Arcane tends to have (speaking generally) -- for example, a percentage chance, a stat buff, and the duration of the buff. 

Certain Arcanes increase all of these stats per rank (making them scale exponentially), but we are changing it so that only one stat is affected by rank (making it scale linearly). The other stats will now be at the max-rank value regardless of the Arcane Rank, thereby buffing lower-rank Arcanes as a result.

'''Pax Charge''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] for [[Kitgun]]s that changes the Magazine type to a [[Reload#Rechargeable weapons|rechargeable battery]], like that of the {{Weapon|Cycron}}. Each rank of the enhancement reduces the recharge delay before ammo can regenerate.

==Effect==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! Rank !! Recharge Delay
|-
| 0 || 12.5%
|-
| 1 || 25%
|-
| 2 || 37.5%
|-
| 3 || 50%
|}

==Acquisition==
Can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|10,000}} per arcane upon reaching the rank of '''Old Mate'''.

==Notes==
*Recharge rate is '''not''' affected by mods or abilities. Recharge rate depends on the chamber part:
{| class="wikitable"
|+ Recharge Rate
|-
! colspan=1 | Chamber
| Primary || Secondary
|-
! {{Weapon|Catchmoon|Catchmoon}}
| 5 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Gaze|Gaze}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Rattleguts|Rattleguts}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Sporelacer|Sporelacer}}
| 5 ammo/sec || 25 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Tombfinger|Tombfinger}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Vermisplicer|Vermisplicer}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 25 ammo/sec
|-
|}
*Similar to [[Archgun]]s and the {{Weapon|Cycron}}, base recharge delay is equal to the reload time displayed on the weapon.
**Reduced reload time (recharge delay) is shown in the [[Arsenal]] upon equipping Pax Charge.
**Recharge delay is further reduced (stacking additively) by reload speed mods like {{M|Quickdraw}} and {{M|Stunning Speed}}.
*Reduces the recharge delay by increasing reload speed. At max rank, it increases the reload speed by 50%, which reduces the recharge delay by 33.3%. See [[Reload Speed]] for the details.
**For example, with a Kitgun that has a reload time of 2.1 seconds:
***Unranked Pax Charge will result in a recharge delay of <math>{
\frac{2.1}{1 + 12.5\%} = 1.87
}</math> seconds, a reduction of 11.1%.
***Rank 3 Pax Charge will result in a recharge delay of <math>{
\frac{2.1}{1 + 50\%} = 1.4
}</math> seconds, a reduction of 33.3%.
*Prevents the weapon from receiving benefit from reload-triggered mods or Arcanes such as {{M|Pressurized Magazine}} or {{Arcane|Arcane Awakening}}.

==Tips==
*Pax Charge is useful for prolonged missions due to never requiring actual ammunition, however this also means you are limited to essentially your original magazine size of ammo before having to recharge.
**[[Carrier]] sentinel, equipped with {{M|Ammo Case}}, is an alternative to keep ammo reserves up in missions, although this requires picking up of ammo and the sentinel to be alive.
**{{M|Pistol Ammo Mutation}} ({{M|Primed Pistol Ammo Mutation|Primed}}) or {{M|Pistol Scavenger}} can be used as alternative as well, at a cost of a mod slot and capacity in a Kitgun or an aura slot in a Warframe, respectively.
*Pax Charge can be used in conjunction with {{M|Synth Charge}} to reload only the last shot in the magazine, however it will often reload multiple shots before the player is able to fire them with semi-auto kitguns.
*A Kitgun equipped with Pax Charge will almost always require a longer time to fully recharge the magazine than the actual normal reload of the weapon.
**The Sporelacer and Catchmoon secondaries, as well as both Tombfinger variants, can recharge faster than the game will automatically reload your weapon. However, there is a [[Reload#Manual Reload|delay]] before the automatic reload starts that can be circumvented by manually reloading, which cannot be performed while using Pax Charge. While this can be circumvented with enough fire rate, it may be impractical to fire the weapons fast enough given their semi-automatic trigger type.
*Recharge delay can be reduced by abilities that affect reload speed, but recharge rate will '''not''' be affected. Recharge delay is affected by:
**{{WF|Chroma}}'s {{A|Elemental Ward}} with {{D|Toxin}} alignment
**{{WF|Volt}}'s {{A|Speed}}
**{{WF|Harrow}}'s {{A|Penance}}
**{{WF|Gauss}}'s {{A|Redline}}
